children.description: Pleurotus cornucopiae is a species of edible fungus in the genus Pleurotus, It is quite similar to the better-known Pleurotus ostreatus, and like that species is cultivated and sold in markets in Europe and China, but it is distinguished because its gills are very decurrent, forming a network on the stem.

children.name: Pleurotus euosmus
children.description: Pleurotus euosmus, also known as tarragon oyster mushroom, is a species of edible fungus in the genus Pleurotus, It is quite similar to the better-known Pleurotus ostreatus, but it is distinguished by its strong smell reminiscent of tarragon and substantially larger spores.

children.name: Pleurotus nebrodensis
children.description: Pleurotus nebrodensis, commonly known as "fungus of basilisk" or "macchia carduncieddu(?)", is a fungus that was declared by the IUCN as critically endangered in 2006.

children.name: Pleurotus opuntiae
children.description: Pleurotus opuntiae is a species of Agaricales fungus that grows in the semi-arid climate of central Mexico and in New Zealand, whose mushroom is edible and considered a delicacy in the cuisine of indigenous peoples of Mexico.

children.name: Pleurotus ostreatus
children.description: Pleurotus ostreatus, commonly known as the oyster mushroom, grey oyster mushroom, oyster fungus, hiratake, or pearl oyster mushroom, is a popular edible mushroom found in temperate and subtropical forests around the world.

children.name: Pleurotus parsonsiae

children.name: Pleurotus populinus
children.description: Pleurotus populinus, the aspen oyster mushroom, is a gilled fungus native to North America.

children.name: Pleurotus pulmonarius
children.description: Pleurotus pulmonarius, commonly known as the Indian oyster, Italian oyster, phoenix mushroom, or the lung oyster, is a mushroom very similar to Pleurotus ostreatus, the pearl oyster, but with a few noticeable differences.
